protocol.description:
The hyprtavern core protocol describes how applications can connect to a hyprtavern bus, expose themselves, and discover other applications running on the same bus.
Permission names and matching rules are defined by Hyprtavern's permission catalog (docs/PERMISSIONS.md in the hyprtavern repository). A malformed permission name in any request is an invalid_permission protocol error. A well-formed name in the reserved core namespace that the tavern does not know is not an error: requests for it fail, and requirements containing it are never satisfied. This lets the catalog grow without breaking older taverns.
Protocol errors raised by the tavern use the codes of protocol_errors.
Later revisions may add values to enums. A sender must only use values defined in the version of the object it bound; an unknown value in a request is an invalid_argument protocol error. Receivers of events must handle unknown values conservatively: unknown identity kinds as unknown, unknown authorities and policies as the least privileged value, and any other unknown value as a failure.
Each array may contain at most 65535 elements. An oversized input array is an invalid_argument protocol error. The tavern must never emit oversized or silently truncated arrays, including query results, metadata, and explicit grant snapshots.
To keep snapshots representable, the bus may have at most 65535 live bus objects in total, across all clients. Each client connection may own at most 512 live bus objects, and each object may expose at most 512 distinct protocols and 512 properties. A request that would exceed these registration limits is a limit_exceeded protocol error and must not be applied. Replacing an existing entry or removing one does not consume an additional slot. Permission grant limits are defined by hp_hyprtavern_permission_context_v1.
Authorization of routed connections is admission-only. The tavern checks permissions before issuing the socket pair and fixes its protocol scope at that point. Later grant changes, context destruction, or disconnection from the tavern neither revoke nor expand an existing connection's scope. A new connection is required to obtain a different scope. Application protocols may define additional authorization for their own operations.
Barmaids are started by the tavern and authenticated through private startup channels. The tavern must reserve the barmaid, kv_store, and permission_authentication protocol names for the corresponding barmaids it started. Neither a claimed name, exclusivity, nor ordinary permission bypass authorizes another provider to register these protocols.

value.name: all
value.description: all names must be present

value.name: any
value.description: any single name must be present

value.name: invalid_argument
value.description: a malformed argument, e.g. an oversized array or an out-of-range enum value

value.name: invalid_state
value.description: a request that is not allowed in the object's current state

value.name: not_ready
value.description: a request sent before the manager's ready event

value.name: invalid_permission
value.description: a malformed permission name, or one that cannot be used in this request

value.name: invalid_property
value.description: a malformed property name or value, or a malformed query property

value.name: limit_exceeded
value.description: a registration limit was exceeded

value.name: applied
value.description: The tavern applied the environment update

value.name: denied
value.description: The caller does not satisfy core.unobtainium.unsandboxed

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_core_manager_v1
object.description: This object is a core manager object bound upon creation.

s2c.name: ready
s2c.description:
This event is emitted once the tavern connection is ready to accept other requests.
Clients must wait on this event before doing anything else, otherwise a not_ready protocol error is raised.

c2s.name: create_permission_context
c2s.description:
Create a permission context that can be used to request permissions.
A client connection may have at most one live permission context, even if multiple managers are bound. Destroying it permits another to be created. Creating a second one is an invalid_state protocol error. Its grants apply to this client connection, not automatically to other connections from the same application.
The tavern associates the context with the caller's attested application identity, including its identity kind. A persistence token selects an independent saved context owned by that identity; it is not a bearer grant. Restoration requires the same stable attested owner. A token belonging to another owner causes unavailable, without restoring any of its data.
Permission contexts use the plaintext session kv_store for persistence. It requires no password or user interaction. If the store is available and the caller has a stable identity, an empty or unknown token creates a new saved context. Unstable or unknown identities may only receive session grants and policy decisions.
An initializing or unavailable store disables restoration and creation of persistent grants, but session grants and policy decisions remain available. A supplied token is retained as an unverified restoration hint, not replaced or trusted. The persistence_token event carries an empty string until a saved context can be verified or created. The client must retain its previous durable token. When the store becomes available, the tavern retries restoration or creation and emits the durable token. Until then, no grants are restored from the token.
The tavern may bypass ordinary permission checks for some principals by policy. Applications must not assume such a policy applies and should request every named permission they require.

arg.name: persistence_token
arg.summary: previously issued persistence token, or empty

c2s.name: redeem_connection_principal_token
c2s.description:
Redeem the connection_principal_token from hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_v1.new_fd to inspect the principal associated with that connection.
The initial snapshot is retained at admission and does not require the originating client or its permission context to remain alive. Redeeming an unexpired, unused token as its intended recipient must still succeed after that client disconnects or destroys its context.

c2s.name: get_bus_object
c2s.description:
Create a bus object on the bus. See hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_v1 for more.
You are allowed to expose multiple objects, but it is discouraged.
object_name does not have to be unique on the bus. It may be at most 256 bytes long; a longer name is an invalid_argument protocol error.
required_permissions supplies the initial object-level visibility and connection requirements. These are applied atomically with creation, so the object is never temporarily public. An empty array imposes no object-level requirements. See require_permissions.

arg.name: object_name
arg.summary: A human-readable, short name for the object

arg.name: required_permissions
arg.summary: initial permissions required to discover or connect to the object

c2s.name: get_query_object
c2s.description:
Create a query object. A query object takes an array of protocol names as input.
Optionally, you can include a list of properties to filter by. If you do not wish to add any, leave the array empty.
Each string in the list of properties must come in the form of (name)=(value), split at the first equals sign. The name and value follow expose_property's rules. An invalid_property error is raised otherwise. Values are matched exactly.
An empty filter array imposes no constraint, regardless of its filter mode. The protocol and property filters must both match. Only objects visible to the caller are returned; empty arrays do not bypass visibility permissions.

arg.name: protocol_names
arg.summary: An array of protocol names to query by

arg.name: protocol_names_filter
arg.summary: Filter mode for the array of protocol names

arg.name: property_list_filter
arg.summary: Filter mode for the array of properties

c2s.name: get_object_handle
c2s.description:
Create an object handle. Given an object ID, this object will return information about the bus object.
IDs identify one registration and must not be reused during the lifetime of a tavern instance. A handle never retargets to a replacement provider.

c2s.name: update_tavern_environment
c2s.description:
Send new environment for the tavern to treat as primary. This will be sent to barmaids as well. Environment like `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` will dictate where barmaids show their GUI elements.
Two arrays dictate names and values respectively, e.g. { "WAYLAND_DISPLAY", "DISPLAY" }, { "wayland-1", ":1" }
An empty value unsets an environment variable.
Setting or unsetting any environment variable requires core.unobtainium.unsandboxed. This includes non-display variables, which can also affect trusted barmaid execution and UI placement. No ordinary permission authorizes environment updates. core.unobtainium.unsandboxed is derived from verified same-user, unsandboxed host status; it cannot be granted by a popup or inferred from ordinary permission bypass.
The arrays must have equal lengths. Names must be nonempty, contain neither '=' nor NUL, and occur at most once; values must not contain NUL. Malformed input is an invalid_argument protocol error. The tavern validates the entire request and checks authorization before applying or forwarding any changes.
A valid but unauthorized request returns update_tavern_environment_result with denied, without changing or forwarding any environment values. This is not a protocol error and does not disconnect the client.
Each valid request receives exactly one update_tavern_environment_result, in request order on this manager, unless the manager is destroyed or the client disconnects first. Empty arrays perform no changes but follow the same authorization and result rules.

arg.name: env_names
arg.summary: An array of environment variable names

arg.name: env_values
arg.summary: An array of environment variable values

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description:
This request destroys the manager. All objects remain valid until they are destroyed.
Existing socket connections are not closed.

s2c.name: update_tavern_environment_result
s2c.description:
Completes the next outstanding update_tavern_environment request on this manager. Results are emitted in request order, including denials.
applied confirms that the tavern committed the update; it is not an acknowledgement from each barmaid that it has processed the forwarded environment. denied leaves the environment unchanged and permits further requests on this connection.

value.name: already_exposed
value.description: registration conflicts with protocol exclusivity

value.name: unauthorized_provider
value.description: provider is not authorized to register this protocol

value.name: invalid_registration
value.description: invalid protocol name, revision, or mandatory infrastructure registration settings

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_v1
object.description: This object is a bus object representing an open, exposed object on the bus.

s2c.name: new_fd
s2c.description:
Another client on the bus requested to connect to this object. The connection must be established on the given incoming FD in SERVER mode.
connection_principal_token is always a short-lived, single-use token bound to this recipient. It can only be redeemed by this object provider with redeem_connection_principal_token to inspect the principal associated with this connection.
The token retains an immutable admission-time snapshot of the principal's identity, authority, permission policy, display identity, and explicit grants until it is redeemed or expires. The originating client's disconnection or permission-context destruction must not invalidate it. After redemption, the principal object retains the admitted identity and authority for its own lifetime; expiry of the consumed token has no effect on that object.
protocol_scope describes which protocols may be used over this fd. The object's provider must install an allowlist before dispatching any input or starting the handshake. Protocols outside the scope must neither be advertised nor be bindable, even if the client guesses their names. The scope cannot change during this connection.
The principal identifies the client to which the tavern issued the fd. It does not attest every subsequent writer: an fd may be inherited or delegated.

s2c.name: expose_protocol_error
s2c.description: Failed to expose the named protocol. The request has no effect; an existing registration on this object, if any, remains unchanged.

c2s.name: expose_protocol
c2s.description:
Explicitly exposes a supported protocol alongside the revision version on the object.
protocol_name must be nonempty and at most 255 bytes long, and version must be greater than zero. Protocol names are otherwise opaque and case-sensitive. Violations produce expose_protocol_error with invalid_registration, without changing state.
This allows other apps to discover and request access to a protocol via the bus.
A protocol will only be available on a connection if it was requested through hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_handle_v1.connect and granted by the tavern. The object provider must apply the protocol_scope from new_fd as an allowlist before dispatching the fd. See new_fd.
The object provider can redeem the connection_principal_token passed in new_fd to inspect the connecting principal before accepting protocol use.
All required_permissions must be satisfied at admission, in addition to the object's requirements. Protocol definitions must document their access requirements so clients can request permissions before connecting.
If exclusive_mode is non-zero, no other object may expose this protocol. An existing exclusive registration also rejects later non-exclusive registrations. Exclusivity is checked and reserved atomically. Conflicts produce expose_protocol_error with already_exposed.
Reserved barmaid protocols may only be registered by their authenticated, tavern-started providers; otherwise unauthorized_provider is returned. Exclusivity alone does not establish a provider's identity or trust.
The kv_store and permission_authentication protocols must be registered exclusively. permission_authentication must additionally include core.unobtainium.tavernkeep in its protocol-level required_permissions; an object-level requirement alone is insufficient. An authenticated provider omitting these settings receives invalid_registration. The tavern must not silently add or repair the missing settings.
The barmaid control protocol is private to startup channels and must never be registered on this application-facing bus.
Exposing the same protocol again on this object atomically replaces its registration if valid. Changes affect new admissions, not existing sockets.

arg.name: required_permissions
arg.summary: canonical permission names required to bind this protocol

c2s.name: expose_property
c2s.description:
Objects can expose properties that help other processes looking for an interface to distinguish objects apart.
These properties can be arbitrary, but should follow standard conventions described in the specific protocols, or global, agreed upon values, e.g. environment.
Used protocol(s) should specify methods of discovery in their descriptions.
Property names must come in the form of (group):(name). Group of "GLOBAL" describes a non-protocol-specific property, e.g. GLOBAL:WAYLAND_DISPLAY. Both group and name must be nonempty ASCII strings containing only letters, numbers, _ or +. Names may be at most 255 bytes long and values at most 4096 bytes. Other names or values are an invalid_property protocol error.
Setting a property value to an empty string removes the property.
Properties must not be used for data that is rapidly changing, and must not be used for "quick data access". All properties are visible to anyone allowed to inspect the object; there are no per-property restrictions. They are provider-supplied discovery hints, not attested identity or authorization data. For data access, you must use a separate protocol.

c2s.name: require_permissions
c2s.description:
Atomically replace the permissions required to discover, inspect, or connect to this object. All listed requirements must be satisfied. An empty array removes object-level requirements. Initial requirements can be set without a public discovery window using get_bus_object.
The core.monitoring.sensitive.all_bus_objects permission permits inspection despite visibility requirements, but does not waive connection requirements. Existing handles do not preserve authorization: requirements are checked again at connection admission. Existing sockets are unaffected.
For fine-grained control, use the required_permissions argument of expose_protocol.

arg.name: required_permissions
arg.summary: canonical permission names required to discover or connect to this object

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description:
This request destroys the object, removes it from discovery, and releases its protocol registrations. Handles to it can no longer admit connections.
Existing socket connections are not closed.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_query_v1
object.description:
This object is a query object returning data about the query.
Immediately after receiving results, destroy should be called to avoid leaking wire protocol objects.

s2c.name: results
s2c.description:
This event returns an array of object IDs that matched the requested query. These IDs can be used with the manager to create a handle and inspect a given object.
Exactly one results event is sent, including when no objects match. It is a snapshot, not a subscription: objects may change or disappear before a handle is obtained. No visibility or connection authorization is reserved. All matches are returned; the bus-wide registration limit ensures that there are at most 65535 IDs, without truncation or pagination.

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: This request destroys the query object.

value.name: unknown_error
value.description: An unknown error occurred

value.name: bad_protocol
value.description: A requested protocol was invalid / missing

value.name: insufficient_permissions
value.description: Object or protocol permission requirements were not satisfied

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_bus_object_handle_v1
object.description:
This object is a handle to an existing bus object. It will return detailed data about the object.
Creation emits either failed, or one coherent snapshot consisting of name, protocols, properties, and provider_identity, followed by done. The order of the snapshot events before done is unspecified. This handle remains bound to the same registration instance even if the provider subsequently exits.

s2c.name: failed
s2c.description:
This event is sent if the bus failed to obtain a given object. This could be due to insufficient permissions, or an object not existing.
This handle is inert and must be destroyed. No further information will be sent and connect is not allowed.

s2c.name: name
s2c.description: This is a human-readable name of the object. It is not unique.

s2c.name: protocols
s2c.description:
This event contains the exposed protocols of the object. Two arrays describe names and revisions.
For example, protocol at protocol_names index 0's max supported version is described by protocol_revs at index 0, and so on.
The arrays have equal lengths and protocol names are unique. Advertising a protocol here does not imply that the caller may connect to it.

s2c.name: properties
s2c.description:
This event contains the exposed properties of the object.
A single array describes the properties in the form of (name)=(value).

c2s.name: connect
c2s.description:
Request connection to the object, on specified protocols. This may be called only once and only after done. A second call, including while the first is pending, is an invalid_state protocol error. Destroy is allowed while a call is pending.
All protocols the client wishes to use must be asked for, otherwise they will be unavailable on this socket.
If any of the protocols are unavailable, inaccessible or otherwise unreachable, socket_failed will be emitted.
The tavern rechecks the registration and all current object and requested protocol requirements before issuing either endpoint. Admission is all-or-nothing; exactly one socket or socket_failed event follows unless the handle is destroyed or the client disconnects first.
This request never opens a permission popup. Clients must explicitly obtain the required permissions before connecting. A stale metadata snapshot or permission result is not a reservation of access.
A client connection may have at most 512 admitted connections whose connection principal tokens are neither redeemed nor expired. Further attempts fail with unknown_error until tokens are redeemed or expire.
An empty protocol_names or duplicate name is an invalid_argument protocol error.

s2c.name: socket
s2c.description:
This event carries the file descriptor to connect to the socket. It will be emitted after .connect is requested.
You must connect to the given fd with hyprwire in CLIENT mode.
After this event is emitted, this object becomes inert. It should be destroyed.

s2c.name: socket_failed
s2c.description:
Emitted if the connection to the object failed. Possible causes include the object being already gone, insufficient permissions, or bad requested protocols.
After this event is emitted, this object becomes inert. It should be destroyed.

arg.name: error
arg.summary: The error that caused the connection to fail

s2c.name: done
s2c.description: The initial metadata snapshot is complete. No further metadata updates will be sent. The handle is now ready for connect and is not inert. Destroy it if no connection is needed.

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: This request destroys the object handle and cancels a connection attempt not yet admitted. It does not revoke a socket already issued.

s2c.name: provider_identity

description.summary: Attested identity of the registered provider

s2c.description:
Reports the tavern-attested application identity of this registration's provider, using the same identity rules as connection_principal.application_identity. The tavern must issue any subsequent socket from this handle to that same registered provider, or fail the connection attempt. A name or property supplied by the provider must never be substituted for this identity.
This authenticates the original provider receiving the endpoint, not any later process to which it delegates the fd. Unknown identity is reported with an empty identifier and stable_across_executions set to zero.

arg.name: stable_across_executions
arg.summary: non-zero if the identity is stable across executions

value.name: session
value.description: Until the permission context is destroyed or its client disconnects

value.name: permanent
value.description: Persisted for restoration by the same owner and token until revoked

value.name: granted
value.description: Explicitly granted

value.name: already_granted
value.description: Already was granted

value.name: granted_by_policy
value.description: Granted because of a policy

value.name: denied
value.description: Explicitly denied

value.name: failed
value.description: Error occurred

value.name: external
value.description: principal represents an external application connection

value.name: internal
value.description: principal was established by the tavern for an internal connection

value.name: unknown
value.description: no application identity could be attested

value.name: host_executable
value.description: identity is an attested executable of a verified same-user, unsandboxed host process

value.name: flatpak
value.description: identity is an attested Flatpak application ID

value.name: internal
value.description: identity is assigned by the tavern to an internal application

value.name: enforced
value.description: ordinary permission checks are enforced

value.name: bypass_ordinary_permissions
value.description: ordinary permission checks are bypassed by policy

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_permission_context_v1
object.description:
This object allows an application to request permissions on the bus and persist grants across sessions.
Session grants last until this context is destroyed or its client connection closes, whichever happens first. They do not authorize other client connections. Expiration or revocation affects future admissions, not existing routed sockets.
The union of session and permanent explicit grants may contain at most 512 distinct permission names. A request that would exceed this limit returns permission_result with failed without adding or persisting a grant. Restoration that would exceed the limit makes the context unavailable; grants must not be partially restored or silently truncated.
Enumeration and revocation of saved grants are outside this protocol's scope and are reserved for a separate permission-management protocol.

s2c.name: unavailable
s2c.description:
This event is emitted if the tavern cannot establish the context, for example because authorization services are not initialized or the supplied token belongs to another identity. It may also follow a deferred restoration that fails its ownership check. No grants remain active through this context.
This object is inert. Destroy it before creating another context to retry. An unavailable store alone does not make a context unavailable: session grants and policy decisions remain possible without persistence.

s2c.name: persistence_token
s2c.description:
Emitted on creation unless unavailable is sent instead. A nonempty token identifies a verified, durably stored context owned by the caller's stable attested identity. It matches the supplied token on successful restoration; otherwise it is a newly generated token, never an adopted unknown input token.
An empty token means no saved context is available yet. It must not replace a token the client previously saved. It conveys no restored permissions. The tavern sends this event again with a nonempty token when deferred restoration or creation succeeds. No retry is possible without a stable attested identity.
Save nonempty tokens for future restoration, preferably as app-scoped KV values. Read any previously saved token before replacing it; a failed or unavailable KV lookup must not be treated as value_missing. Losing a token loses the reference to that saved context, not its stored grants. A token does not promise that future writes will succeed; permission_result reports whether a grant was actually persisted.

arg.name: persistence_token
arg.summary: durable restoration token, or empty without a saved context

c2s.name: set_display_identity
c2s.description:
This optional request provides human-readable strings for presenting this application to the user.
These strings are self-asserted by the application. They are not an attested application identity and must not be used for authorization. The name may be at most 256 bytes and the description at most 2048 bytes long; longer strings are an invalid_argument protocol error.
This data is saved with the context when persistence is available; otherwise it remains session-only. Updating it must not alter an already pending prompt.

c2s.name: request_permission
c2s.description:
This request asks the bus to grant a given permission to this object.
This may pop up an interactive box to the user.
core.unobtainium.unsandboxed never prompts: it returns granted_by_policy for verified same-user unsandboxed host clients and denied otherwise, regardless of ordinary permission bypass. It is never a saved or explicit grant.
This request can succeed, or fail. If the permission is already granted, it's treated as a success.
Permissions are identified by canonical dotted names. A permission group may define a canonical catch-all name for all permissions within that group. core.unobtainium.tavernkeep is not requestable; requesting it is an invalid_permission protocol error. A core permission the tavern does not know returns failed.
permission_result will be emitted some time after this request to indicate a success or failure. A client must not assume it has a permission before permission_result is received.
At most one request for a given permission_name may be pending on this context. A duplicate pending request is an invalid_state protocol error; different names may be requested concurrently. At most 512 requests may be pending on a context; further requests return permission_result with failed. Each request receives exactly one result unless the context becomes unavailable, is destroyed, or its client disconnects.
ask_mode is the maximum lifetime requested. A permanent request may yield a session grant if the user chooses it or persistence is unavailable; the actual lifetime is reported in permission_result. A session request must not create a new permanent grant. Existing permanent grants may be reused.

arg.name: ask_mode
arg.summary: In what way to ask for the permission

s2c.name: permission_result
s2c.description:
This event completes the request with the matching permission_name. grant_mode gives the actual lifetime for granted and already_granted. permanent may only be reported after the grant is durably stored under this context's verified owner and token. A failed persistence write must not be reported as a permanent grant.
For granted_by_policy, denied, and failed, grant_mode is session and has no grant-lifetime meaning. Policy decisions are not stored explicit grants.

arg.name: grant_mode
arg.summary: actual lifetime of an explicit grant, otherwise session

c2s.name: destroy
c2s.description: Destroys this context, cancels pending prompts, and stops using its grants for future admissions. Saved grants are not deleted and existing sockets are unaffected. Results processed before this request are not undone.

object.name: hp_hyprtavern_connection_principal_v1
object.description:
This object reports the identity and authorization state the tavern associated with a connection. Each successful query emits one authority, process_identity, application_identity, display_identity, and explicit_permission_grants event, followed by done.
Identity is associated with the original admitted client, not inferred from the routed socket's peer credentials. Identity kind and identifier together identify the application; neither a display label nor PID is a substitute.
The initial snapshot is the admission-time snapshot retained by the token, even if the originating client or context no longer exists. Requery may report current permission policy, display identity, and grants while live state is available. The admitted process identity, application identity, and authority remain fixed; PID reuse or a replacement client connection must never retarget this object to another principal.

s2c.name: authority
s2c.description:
Reports how the principal was established and whether ordinary permission checks apply. bypass_ordinary_permissions is a policy decision; it does not imply that every permission name is explicitly granted.
authority is fixed at admission. permission_policy is the admission-time policy in the initial snapshot and the current policy on successful requery.

s2c.name: process_identity
s2c.description:
Reports the process ID observed by the tavern for this connection. A process ID is transient and is not an application identity.
This is the PID in the tavern's process namespace at admission. It may no longer refer to the original process and must not be used for authorization.

s2c.name: application_identity
s2c.description:
Reports the application identity attested by the tavern, not a string supplied by the application. attested_app_id is interpreted according to identity_kind. stable_across_executions is non-zero only when this identity is stable across executions.
host_executable guarantees that the admitted process was positively verified as unsandboxed and had the same effective UID as the tavern. It attests core.unobtainium.unsandboxed independently of permission_policy, including when ordinary permission bypass is disabled. Missing or ambiguous sandbox information must never be reported as host_executable.
Unknown identity has an empty identifier and stable_across_executions equal to zero. Unknown or unstable identities cannot own persistent app-scoped state.

arg.name: stable_across_executions
arg.summary: non-zero if the attested identity is stable across executions

s2c.name: display_identity
s2c.description: Reports optional, human-readable strings supplied by the application. These strings are not attested and must not be used for authorization. Use application_identity for the tavern-attested identity.

s2c.name: explicit_permission_grants
s2c.description:
Reports only canonical permission names explicitly granted to this principal. Each name appears at most once, with at most 512 names in total. Policy bypass is reported separately by authority and must not be inferred from this list. An empty list does not negate a bypass_ordinary_permissions policy.
The initial snapshot reports grants at admission, which may no longer be active when this event is received. Successful requery reports current grants. Neither snapshot is a list of protocols authorized on the fd. Later changes to these grants do not change the admission-time protocol_scope. core.unobtainium.unsandboxed is derived from host status and is never in this list.

s2c.name: done
s2c.description: All data for the current snapshot has been sent.

s2c.name: failed

description.summary: Failed to redeem or query the principal

s2c.description:
The token was invalid, expired, already used, redeemed by the wrong recipient, or the principal could not be queried. This object is now inert and should be destroyed.
Initial redemption must not fail merely because the originating client disconnected or its permission context was destroyed: the token retains the admission snapshot. A later requery may fail if live state is unavailable.

c2s.name: requery
c2s.description:
Principal data can change over time. After done, this request sends a new complete snapshot, terminated by done, on this object. Only one snapshot may be pending; requesting another before done, or requerying an inert principal, is an invalid_state protocol error.
Unlike initial redemption, requery requires live state for the original principal and may fail after its client disconnects or context is destroyed. A failed query does not invalidate the previously received admission identity.
Requery is informational, not reauthorization of the existing fd. Neither a changed grant list nor a failed query revokes or expands its original scope.
